D.t: Phil Weiser leads by 20.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 573,730 votes; a one point swing is about 14,187 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +11.0 and D +29.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +16.5. Your best recent poll is University of Colorado/YouGov at D +19.2; your worst is Lake Research Partners (D) at D +12.0. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 233,659 votes; Boulder, a projected net 115,607 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 96,629 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +2.9, 11.8% of the vote; Douglas, R +0.7, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +2.4, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +9.0, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Weiser runs furthest behind in Weld, Douglas, El Paso. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.09 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Incomes $50K to $124K, 54% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.69 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Phil Weiser: Immigration voters 25 to 73, Small counties 46 to 51, Midsize counties 49 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$725K cash against $158K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
